articles.title: ‘I struggle to see myself as someone special’: Sandra Hüller on being the star of four - or, possibly, five - of the year’s biggest films
articles.summary: New film Fatherland took Sandra Hüller back to a divided Germany. She talks about damaged dreams, Hollywood feelgood and - just maybe - appearing in the new Marvel movie. Sandra Hüller is crying, and it feels very strange. A wildly gifted actor, she can convey every human emotion there is.
body: And yet, dressed in film star black, she is in tears. “This is really hard for me,” she says.

We are talking about Fatherland. Directed by acclaimed Polish film-maker Paweł Pawlikowski, Hüller plays the German polymath Erika Mann, who in the film drives her novelist father Thomas Mann through newly divided postwar Germany. The Nazi past shadows everything – but the movie is also tied up with the birth of East Germany, where Hüller grew up. (She still lives in what was once the GDR.) I tell her I’ve never before seen a film that acknowledged the utopian dreams of that place and time, however damaged they became. Yes, she replies: German directors don’t know how to approach it.
“But Fatherland has a grief that you feel clearer coming from the East.”

And then her voice cracks, and she cries. We reflexively apologise to each other. “I’m just grateful Pawel gave space to this political idea that didn’t survive in Germany, but is one maybe people can still think about. The socialist idea.”

body: Netflix, ‘Elite’ star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll are adapting Clarín’s classic novel into a feature film which went into production Oct. 23, produced by María Zamora at Elastica Films (“Alcarràs” “Romería”).
The current adaptation will be a new contemporary version that reinterprets the classic from a “fresh female perspective,” Netflix announced Friday.

“La Regenta” marks Netflix’s latest venture into revered big literary IP in the Spanish-speaking world after adaptations of Gabriel García Márquez’s “One Hundred Years of Solitude” on Colombia and “The Eternaut” in Argentina. Both were Netflix Global Top 10 non-English hits and signature shows for the U.S. streaming giant.

Published over 1884-85, “La Regenta” turns on Ana Ozores, young, beautiful and married off to Victor Quintanar, a man twice her age and ex magistrate of Vetusta, a sleepy stifling provincial city where, says Netflix “everything is known and everything is judged.”

articles.title: Asif Kapadia on Bringing the ‘Profound’ ‘7 Up’ Documentary Series to a Close After More Than 60 Years: ‘It’s a Dream Job’
articles.summary: From a charismatic Formula 1 racing legend to a brilliant but flawed soccer god to a troubled, tragic singer, Academy Award-winning docmaker Asif Kapadia has made a career out of telling the stories of larger-than-life figures.
body: The “Up” series of films launched in 1964 with “7 Up,” capturing the lives of 10 boys and four girls in England all aged seven at the time. Cameras then revisited the group every seven years to chart their journey from childhood to teenagers, to adulthood, through careers, marriage, divorce, parenting, bereavement and more.
The longest-running documentary series ever made, it’s been broadcast in 157 countries, including the U.S., Canada, Japan, China, Australia and France.

All but the first in the series were directed by Michael Apted, who passed away in 2021. Kapadia was handed the baton to direct the final installment, saying he “felt very honored and privileged to have a chance to be a part of it.”
“It was like finishing off something someone had started — just closing the circle,” he said. “It’s a dream job.”

articles.title: ‘The Notebook’ Musical Sets West End Run at Newly Renamed Judi Dench Theatre
articles.summary: “The Notebook” musical is coming to London’s West End. The show, based on Nicholas Sparks’ bestselling novel and subsequent hit film starring Rachel McAdams and Ryan Gosling, will be the first production at the newly renamed Judi Dench Theatre (previously the Shaftesbury Theatre).
body: “The Notebook” musical originally premiered on Broadway in March 2024 and ran through December, with a U.S. tour following. It received three Tony nominations: best actor for Dorian Harewood, actress for Maryann Plunkett and book of a musical for Brunstetter. The West End cast has yet to be announced.

“The thing that makes a musical so special for me is the collaborative nature of it, and I can’t imagine a better team of people to have built ‘The Notebook,'” Michaelson said. “Getting to revisit and revitalize the piece with Bekah, Michael, Schele and the rest of the team for this new production in London is such an honor, and for our musical to be the first at the newly named Judi Dench Theatre is beyond thrilling.”

Added Brunstetter, “It’s been such a joy to adapt ‘The Notebook’ for the stage — it’s such a timeless, universal love story that speaks to so many aspects of life. Ingrid and I have loved expanding the story so that it truly sings and reaches even more people. We can’t wait to get back in the room with our brilliant creative team and discover this musical all over again for the London audience.”

articles.title: Rebel Wilson secures another Australian court win as co-producers of The Deb awarded just $10
articles.summary: NSW supreme court judge otherwise dismisses case brought by film’s co-producers and awards Wilson almost $400,000 after star countersued. Rebel Wilson has been ordered to pay A$10 (US$7, £5) in damages after emerging victorious from a bitter legal spat with her latest film’s co-producers.
body: The Pitch Perfect star directed, co-produced and starred in The Deb, a musical comedy that became the battleground for multiple legal battles in Australia and the US.
Filmed on a $22m budget, The Deb made just $335,000 (US$235,000, £175,284) at the local box office and is yet to screen outside Oceania.
Wilson’s co-producers allege that shortfall could be traced to her false and derogatory statements about them online.

The Bridesmaids star claimed in July 2024 that producers Amanda Ghost, Gregor Cameron and Vince Holden tried to block The Deb’s release, embezzled money, and behaved inappropriately towards the film’s star, Charlotte MacInnes.
points: NSW supreme court judge otherwise dismisses case brought by film’s co-producers and awards Wilson almost $400,000 after star countersued.

articles.title: Biographies of John Williams and Bernard Herrmann Among Honored Works in ASCAP’s Awards for Music Writing and Broadcasts
articles.summary: The winners of annual awards given out by ASCAP for the year’s most outstanding music writing and broadcasts include biographies of film composers John Williams and Bernard Herrmann, as well as a documentary about cult R&B artist Swamp Dogg, liner notes for an archival release from Frank Zappa…
body: Another book award in the concert music field, this one outside the realm of film music, went to Lucy Caplan for “Dreaming in Ensemble: How Black Artists Transformed American Opera.” Awards for books in the pop music field were given to Gayle Wald for “This Is Rhythm: Ella Jenkins, Children’s Music, and the Long Civil Rights Movement” and James O’Leary for The Middlebrow Musical: Between Broadway and Opera in 1940s America.”

Among the articles that won recognition from the ASCAP judges were a piece by the New York Times’ Ben Sisario about efforts to rescue decaying master tapes, a story by Esteban Meneses about Mexican symphonic composers and an article by the New York Times’ Max Keller about cellists debating the right way to hold their instruments. A piece in the Atlantic by Gabriel Kahana won for outstanding music criticism.
The top broadcast award went to Gail Wein for her podcast series “Classical Gas,” with a special recognition honor for Beato for his YouTube series “Everything Music.”

articles.title: James Bond finalists to screen-test for role this week – reports
articles.summary: Actors in the mix to play 007 in Denis Villeneuve’s installment include Callum Turner and Jack Lowden. The search for the next James Bond may finally be nearing its end: according to reports, a very select group of actors will screen-test to become the next British agent 007 this weekend.
body: According to the Hollywood Reporter and Variety, citing several sources, a group of actors reportedly including Callum Turner and Slow Horses’ Jack Lowden, will appear in front of cameras as the secret agent this weekend in London.

The tests supposedly include three elements: stunts, camera presence and dialogue. Reports vary that between three and five actors are finalists for the role, which was vacated by Daniel Craig after 2021’s No Time to Die. Despite speculation to the contrary, Sinners’ Jack O’Connell and Wuthering Heights star Jacob Elordi are not testing, according to the Hollywood Reporter.

Dune film-maker Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next installment of the Bond franchise for Amazon MGM studios, which bought the series rights as part of an $8.45bn (£6.9bn) deal in 2022. The Peaky Blinders writer Steven Knight will pen the script.
points: Actors in the mix to play 007 in Denis Villeneuve’s installment include Callum Turner and Jack Lowden.

articles.title: Slade star Dave Hill's debut album honours city
articles.summary: Slade legend Dave Hill's first solo album celebrates Wolverhampton roots and personal stories.
body: Slade star Dave Hill is set to release his debut solo album, paying homage to some of his old haunts in Wolverhampton.
Named Dirty Foot Lane, the 10-track album was named after a road near his childhood home and not far from where he lives today.
He collaborated with Noddy Holder's son, Django Holder, on the project, his first since the break-up of the band behind hits such as Merry Xmas Everybody.
"It's got a lot of depth to it, every one of those tracks is a true story about someone close or someone I've lost," he told BBC Radio WM.

articles.title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story
articles.summary: The musical is seen by more than 12 million people worldwide after starting in Stratford-upon-Avon.
body: A musical that began life as a Christmas production in Stratford-upon-Avon has become one of the biggest theatre successes of the century as it celebrates 15 years in London's West End.

Matilda The Musical, which is now the 10th longest-running musical in West End history, has been seen by more than 12 million people around the world, staged more than 10,000 performances and played in more than 100 cities.
Composer and lyricist Tim Minchin said he was still amazed by the show's success.
"Probably the biggest family musical of this century is written by [us] couple of idiots," he joked.
points: The musical is seen by more than 12 million people worldwide after starting in Stratford-upon-Avon.

articles.title: Nana Patekar obituary
articles.summary: Indian actor known for his roles in Salaam Bombay! and the Bollywood hits Parinda and Krantiveer, who had a controversial personal life. The Indian actor Nana Patekar, who has died of a heart attack aged 75, first broke through in Mira Nair’s Salaam Bombay!
body: Until that point, Patekar’s rougher edges had mostly been celebrated. As an actor, he demonstrated a baggy-eyed naturalism that spoke more to Bombay streetlife than Bollywood fantasy. He was given to writing out his dialogue until he had internalised it, and his growling line readings were both idiosyncratic and much imitated. Satyajit Ray counted among the actor’s most illustrious admirers, but apparently could not find a suitable project for him; Patekar instead had Nair to thank for launching him to international prominence in Salaam Bombay! as Baba Golub, the brutal pimp and drug dealer lording over an army of street children.

articles.title: What books had people turning pages and turning up the volume this year?
articles.summary: Thrillers, self-help books and Harry Potter were the big winners for readers from Libraries NI data.
body: Thrillers, self-help books and Harry Potter were among the favourites for readers in Northern Ireland this year, according to Libraries NI.
For those who prefered to listen to their fiction, Freida McFadden had eight of her titles featuring in the top 10 adult fiction audiobooks borrowed.
Jillian McFrederick from Libraries NI said books with "short chapters" and "catchy, racy" themes seemed to be most popular.
But when it came to younger readers, there was little change with Harry Potter continuing to be popular - almost 30 years after the release of the first book.
